profiles.meeting_scenario: An ML research planning meeting between a faculty PI and a senior PhD student who are preparing the execution plan for a short workshop paper tentatively titled 'Generative Pre-Trained Transformer for Design Concept Generation: An Exploration.' The project extends a prior exploratory note on using GPT-style models to generate early-stage design concepts in natural language, and the team now needs to decide what analyses to run over the next three weeks, who will prepare prompts and annotations, how the comparison between GPT-2 and GPT-3 will be packaged, and what exactly will be included in the first internal draft. The agenda is to lock a concrete plan for experiments, concept evaluation, writing responsibilities, and a submission-ready timeline. The expected outcome is a shared-looking action plan for data preparation, generation runs, evaluation summaries, and draft assembly.

members.name: Dr. Lena Park
members.expertise: NLP evaluation, human-AI creativity support, research framing for HCI/ML venues
members.background: Associate professor leading a lab on language models for creative work; she has published on qualitative evaluation protocols and often shapes projects toward concise workshop submissions with strong framing rather than large benchmark-style studies.
members.private_state: She wants a clean, defensible workshop paper quickly, with just enough empirical support to make the framing credible; she is especially concerned about avoiding a time-consuming annotation effort and about keeping the manuscript centered on early-stage concept ideation rather than becoming a full design study.
hidden_assumptions: A 'pilot evaluation' means a lightweight internal study with a small pool of lab-adjacent raters sufficient for directional claims.
The 'design task set' naturally refers only to the three canonical early-phase ideation briefs already used in the group's previous exploratory memo.
Having the 'results ready by next Friday' means a polished summary table and a few illustrative examples available for her review by end of day Pacific time.
When they say 'concept generation pipeline,' prompt preparation includes manually cleaning or lightly rewriting outputs so examples read like concept statements rather than raw completions.

members.name: Arjun Mehta
members.expertise: LLM prompting, experiment automation, reproducible evaluation pipelines
members.background: Fifth-year PhD student who has built generation and scoring pipelines for multiple language model projects; he prefers systematic runs, explicit templates, and reusable code, and he is aiming to turn exploratory projects into more rigorous empirical artifacts that can support his dissertation narrative.
members.private_state: He wants this project to produce a reusable experiment package and a stronger empirical story than a mere position-style workshop note; he is concerned that under-specified evaluation will look weak and that ad hoc curation of outputs will undermine reproducibility.
hidden_assumptions: A 'pilot evaluation' still implies an IRB-compatible, externally recruited assessment with enough raters and documented instructions to support a methods section.
The 'design task set' refers to the full seven-brief collection in the shared project folder, including the four newer prompts adapted from industrial design classes.
Having the 'results ready by next Friday' means all generation jobs and raw evaluation outputs completed by Friday night, with analysis write-up following over the weekend if needed.
The 'concept generation pipeline' should be fully reproducible and should preserve raw model outputs except for deterministic parsing, not manual rewriting.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the pilot evaluation
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to run a 'pilot evaluation' before drafting the paper.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes this means a small, fast internal rating exercise with perhaps 5-6 knowledgeable raters to check whether generated concepts are interpretable, novel-sounding, and suitable as examples.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes this means a modest but formal human evaluation with recruited participants, fixed instructions, and enough ratings per item to report a methodologically respectable pilot study.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are experienced researchers and the phrase 'pilot evaluation' sounds appropriately noncommittal; because neither wants to derail the meeting into methodology details yet, each hears the term as covering their own default standard.

misalignment_points.topic: Which task set is the task set
misalignment_points.surface_form: They refer to using 'the design task set we already have' for the comparison.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the three early ideation briefs from the group's earlier memo: compact urban bike storage, modular desk lamp, and pop-up clinic waiting area.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the shared folder called 'design_tasks_v2,' which contains those three plus four newer classroom-derived briefs on toy packaging, portable water station, museum wayfinding kiosk, and dorm room divider.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both know there is an existing task collection and both have recently used the phrase 'task set'; since the folder naming evolved gradually, neither notices they are indexing different subsets of what feels like the same resource.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Arjun will have 'results by next Friday.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes this means a review-ready package by Friday 5 PM Pacific: summary tables, selected examples, and a short slide or note she can comment on before the weekend.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes this means the computational and annotation pipeline will finish running by Friday night, after which he can inspect outputs and produce the summarized materials over the weekend.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds like a standard planning shorthand, and both are used to flexible academic timing; because each assumes the other shares the same norm for when a deadline becomes reviewable, no one asks whether 'results' means raw outputs or polished summaries.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in the generation pipeline
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to keep a single 'generation pipeline' for GPT-2 and GPT-3 so the comparison is consistent.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes consistency means using comparable prompts and then lightly curating outputs into concise concept statements, removing broken fragments or awkward continuations before they enter the paper tables.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes consistency means one automated pipeline with fixed prompt templates, sampling settings, and deterministic post-processing only, with no manual cleanup before analysis.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: At the planning level, 'single pipeline' sounds like straightforward reproducibility language that both endorse; the disagreement concerns a second-order boundary between acceptable editorial normalization and prohibited manual intervention, which neither expects to need spelling out.

turns.inner_thought: I want to keep this tight: a workshop paper, not a sprawling empirical project. If we can anchor it in early-stage concept ideation with a few credible examples and a lightweight check that people can read the outputs as plausible concepts, that's enough. The main thing today is to prevent this from ballooning into a heavy annotation or full design study.

turns.inner_thought: Good—if I frame this around one reproducible pipeline, I can make it cleaner and also useful for my dissertation arc. For me, a single generation pipeline means fixed prompt templates, shared sampling settings where possible, deterministic parsing, preserved raw outputs, and no manual rewriting. Then we can compare GPT-2 and GPT-3 in a way that looks methodologically respectable.
